evidence_quote: 33 elementary schools in the Beaverton School District in Oregon were randomly assigned to either treatment or control conditions.
resolved_title: The Beaverton School District Arts for Learning (A4L) Lessons Project: Student Impact Findings from Years 1, 2, and 3 (WestEd, 2015)
notes: School-level RCT (32 schools analyzed, matched pairs). Confirmatory sample is all grade 3-5 students enrolled in the schools before random assignment; only students with under 40 percent regular-classroom instruction were excluded. No need criterion for schools.

evidence_quote: To participate in the study, schools must have housed at least one grade between grades 4 and 8, and at least 80 percent of a school’s mathematics and science teachers must have agreed to participate.
evidence_location: PDF p. 24, Executive Summary, Study design
resolved_title: Evaluation of the Effectiveness of the Alabama Math, Science, and Technology Initiative (AMSTI). Final Report (NCEE 2012-4008, February 2012)
notes: recoded after re-retrieval 2026-09-18: first page names Newman, Finney, Bell, Turner, Jaciw, Zacamy, and Feagans Gould (NCEE 2012-4008, February 2012), matching Kraft's citation string; the study-list surname fields (dumont, trautwein, ludtke, neumann, niggli) are wrong in Kraft's data. Eighty-two schools were selected from 144 eligible schools that applied to the AMSTI program, chosen in matched pairs to be representative of their regions on achievement, minority share, and low-income share, then randomized within pairs; all students in grades 4 to 8 of participating teachers are in the sample. Applicant schools are volunteers, not selected on need (tie-breaker 6). Kraft's n 18,713 and 18,710 match the math and reading analytic samples in the report tables.

evidence_quote: The four Writing Project sites, in turn, recruited districts in their service areas with high proportions of ELs in grades 7-12 and a desire to implement the intervention.
resolved_title: The Pathway to Academic Success: Scaling Up a Text-Based Analytical Writing Intervention for Latinos and English Learners in Secondary School (JEP 2020, accepted manuscript)
notes: Districts selected for high EL share; teachers randomized; focal classes were all grade 7-12 ELA and ELD classes except self-contained SPED and introductory ELD. Kraft's two effects (0.38, 0.30) are the EL and non-EL subgroup effects in the two-consecutive-year sample (n 353 + 505 = 858, p. 55), so mixed_samples = 1. Same trial as 1017.

evidence_quote: Participating schools were matched into similar pairs and randomly assigned to either continue with the current algebra curriculum for 2 years or to adopt Cognitive Tutor Algebra I (CTAI), which uses a personalized, mastery-learning, blended-learning approach.
resolved_title: Effectiveness of Cognitive Tutor Algebra I at Scale

evidence_quote: To be eligible to participate, all districts had to meet the federal definition of rural districts.

evidence_quote: The research team recruited schools in five districts that volunteered to participate in the study and these schools entered the study over the course of two years

evidence_quote: Each study addressed both replicability of findings and robustness across Texas settings, with varied teacher characteristics (backgrounds, knowledge, attitudes) and student characteristics (demographics, levels of prior mathematics knowledge).
resolved_title: Integration of Technology, Curriculum, and Professional Development for Advancing Middle School Mathematics
notes: Abstract describes three SimCalc studies (two teacher-level RCTs) in Texas grade 7-8 math but states no student or school eligibility rule; WWC sample characteristics not reported. Likely volunteer teachers with whole classes, but that is not stated, so unclear.

evidence_quote: Non-EL students (those with no matching CELDT score) whose unique identifiers were matched with state achievement test scores in ELA were separated into two subgroups: those who were proficient in ELA (scored at or above the state-established proficiency cut score) and those who were not proficient (scored below the cut score).
resolved_title: Accommodations for English Language Learner Students: The Effect of Linguistic Modification of Math Test Item Sets (NCEE 2009-4079)
notes: Test-accommodation experiment, not an instructional intervention. Full tested sample was all grade 7-8 students in volunteer math classes in 13 California middle schools from districts with 25 percent or more Spanish-speaking ELs (analytic n 4,617: EL 1,214, NEP 1,625, EP 1,778). Kraft's n 2,839 = EL + NEP exactly, so the effect comes from ELs plus non-ELs below the ELA proficiency cut; coded on that subgroup per codebook section 1 and tie-breaker 1, with mixed_samples = 1.

evidence_quote: Eligibility for participation in the study included students who scored at least two years below grade level on the Gates-MacGinitie (GMRT) 4th Edition when in the sixth and seventh grades.
resolved_title: Evaluation Report/Impact Study: Virginia Striving Readers Intervention Initiative (VSRII) (RMC Research, March 2012)

evidence_quote: Schools were eligible to apply for the study if they were in the bottom third of the achievement distribution for the California state standardized test (p. 218).

evidence_quote: all students with consent to participate who were enrolled in a randomized teacher's classroom at the time of post-testing were eligible for inclusion in the analytic sample.

notes: Teachers volunteered and were randomized within schools (tie-breaker 6); students were whole classes with parental consent for data. 31 schools in nine Florida districts, no need criterion.

evidence_quote: Stanford University's Education Program for Gifted Youth (EPGY) conducted a randomized-treatment experiment during the 2006-2007 school year to test the efficacy, for Title I students, of the technological and individualized EPGY Kindergarten through Grade 5 Mathematics Course Sequence, modified for the Title I schools.

evidence_quote: The student scores Minimal or Basic on the Wisconsin Knowledge and Concepts Examination (WKCE) during fall 2009.

evidence_quote: The analytic sample in KIPP middle schools in the lottery-based design includes 891 students, comprising a treatment group of 459 students offered admission and a control group of 432 students not offered admission.

evidence_quote: A total of 1,232 fourth- and fifth-grade students from 61 classrooms in 24 schools completed the study.

evidence_quote: To be selected, schools (and their districts) had to serve high numbers of ELs [...] In the selected schools, all eighth-grade social studies teachers participated, and their class sections were randomly assigned to the treatment or comparison condition.
resolved_title: Improving Content Knowledge and Comprehension for English Language Learners: Findings From a Randomized Control Trial (Journal of Educational Psychology, 2017, 109(1), 22-34; ERIC ED652174 author manuscript)
notes: recoded after re-retrieval 2026-09-18: first page (after a one-line ERIC resubmission note) is the JEP 2017 article naming Vaughn, Martinez, Wanzek, Roberts, Swanson, and Fall, the study Kraft's WWC row cites. Seven middle schools in three districts were recruited because they served high numbers of English learners, every class had to contain at least one EL, and all eighth-grade U.S. history sections were randomized within teacher; 1,629 students, 26.7 percent current or recent ELs, with no student-level rule, so level is school. ES 0.40 is the content knowledge (ASK) effect for the full sample. Kraft's n 1,236 does not appear in the text (1,629 assigned, 224 lost to attrition), probably the WWC analytic sample; the sample is the same, so mixed_samples 0. The quote omits an em dash in the source between its two clauses.

evidence_quote: we compare the fourth- and fifth-grade reading outcomes of students with severe reading difficulties who were provided a researcher-developed treatment with reading outcomes of students in a business-as-usual (BAU) comparison condition.

resolved_title: WWC Single Study Review of Improving Reading Comprehension and Social Studies Knowledge in Middle School (August 2013)
